components.cost_effect: Two exact values and one Gaussian vector per estimator; the base value also supports output selection.
components.goal: Provide an unbiased gradient estimate for f_mu using exact function values.
components.key_estimate: E[g_mu(x,u)]=grad f_mu(x); E||g_mu(x,u)||^2<=L0^2(n+4)^2 under the selected convex global-Lipschitz assumptions.
components.name: One-sided Gaussian finite difference
components.operation: At x, sample u~N(0,I_n) and return [f(x+mu u)-f(x)]u/mu.
components.requires: mu>0, global value access and the stated Gaussian distribution; selected geometry B=I.
transfer_checks: Re-establish unbiasedness, second moment and smoothing bias if values are noisy, queries are restricted, directions change or the geometry changes.

limitations.statement: Unbounded Gaussian trial points require value access outside Q; feasible-only value access is not covered.

The O(n^2 L0^2 R^2/epsilon^2) tuning is an upper guarantee for this selected Algorithm. It does not establish unrestricted Oracle Complexity or a lower bound. The sharper RS_0 result uses a directional-derivative Oracle.

performance_links.scope_note: Theorem 6 bound and source best-iterate guarantee for this exact finite-value model; no unrestricted optimality claim.

variants.cost: For the explicitly stated inclusive run k=0,...,N: at most 2(N+1) exact function-value calls, N+1 exact projections and N+1 independent n-dimensional Gaussian draws. Best-iterate selection reuses the a_k values and needs at most N comparisons. Trial-point formation, scalar-vector products and incumbent storage incur ordinary arithmetic/storage costs; the cost of projection or Gaussian generation is not absorbed into value-query complexity. The unused final update may be omitted in an implementation, but that saving is not used in this budget.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p10 (30), pp14–15 (38)–(39), p16 best-iterate definition, pp16–17 Theorem 6 (45) and (46)
variants.name: RS_mu with mu>0 and B=I
variants.output: hat{x}_N in argmin{f(x_k):0<=k<=N}; choose the earliest index in a tie as a deterministic implementation convention. It belongs to Q. No weighted-average adapter is included.
public_inputs: Dimension n>=1, nonempty closed convex Q subset R^n with exact Euclidean projection, fixed x0 in Q, smoothing radius mu>0 and prescribed positive deterministic steps h_k.
For accuracy tuning: epsilon>0, known L0>0 satisfying the global Lipschitz inequality, and R>0 with ||x0-x*||<=R for some constrained minimizer x*.
variants.query_and_update: For k=0,...,N sample u_k~N(0,I_n) independently of all previous directions. Query a_k=f(x_k) and b_k=f(x_k+mu u_k). Form g_k=((b_k-a_k)/mu)u_k. Update the incumbent using a_k. Set x_{k+1}=proj_Q(x_k-h_k g_k). The final x_{N+1} is generated but is not among the output candidates.
variants.requirements: f:R^n->R is finite, convex and globally L0-Lipschitz in the ordinary Euclidean norm. A constrained minimizer x* in Q exists. Exact f values are available at every requested point in R^n, including points outside Q. Projection onto Q and iid N(0,I_n) sampling are available. This is the paper's B=I specialization.
variants.state_and_initialization: Start at deterministic x0 in Q. Maintain x_k and the best measured iterate and value. Fix mu>0. For a finite run choose integer N>=0 and h_0,...,h_N>0 before sampling directions.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: For an arbitrary prescribed horizon use any fixed mu>0 and positive deterministic steps and apply Theorem 6. For target epsilon>0, L0>0 and R>0, use 0<mu<=epsilon/(2L0 sqrt(n)), N=ceil(4(n+4)^2 L0^2 R^2/epsilon^2), and h_k=R/((n+4)L0 sqrt(N+1)). This is integer rounding of the horizon displayed in (46). Execute k=0,...,N and return the incumbent. No adaptive stopping guarantee is asserted. The general method also permits L0=0; the displayed accuracy tuning is only for L0>0 and R>0.

title: Projected exact-value Gaussian random search
use_when: Use exact function values on all of R^n and an exact projection to minimize a globally Lipschitz convex function; finite noisy or feasible-only value Oracles require different analysis.
